rules: Distinct approvers MUST be distinct human principals, not merely distinct sessions or approval identities of the same person.
An incident opener MUST NOT be the sole releaser for the same incident when dual approval is required.
An impersonation session MUST NOT approve, acknowledge, or release an incident.
A break-glass invoker MUST NOT satisfy the distinct second approver requirement for the same incident action.
Where finance surfaces are affected, at least one approver or acknowledger MUST possess the relevant finance authority required by GOV-0 and platform policy.
Distinct approval identities MUST map to distinct human principals.
Approval or release via impersonation_session is forbidden.
Where dual approval is required, one principal MUST NOT satisfy both approver slots via multiple devices, sessions, or auth surfaces.
If the opener also acts as approver or releaser under exceptional policy, explicit justification and post-incident review are mandatory.

Any node, process, or readiness surface that can touch sensitive incident-affected flows MUST start in deny-by-default privileged posture until active incident state and freeze posture are loaded and acknowledged.
A node MAY remain degraded_alive or buyer_limited_ready without being terminated, but it MUST NOT advertise privileged readiness until the required barriers pass.
If authoritative incident posture cannot be loaded, the node MUST emit incident readiness failure telemetry and remain in degraded_alive or stricter posture rather than crash-loop by default.
Privileged readiness MUST be withheld until incident posture synchronization reaches the required convergence target for the affected plane.
Readiness state MUST bind to interactive_upgrade_barriers so degraded_alive never behaves like full interactive readiness.

changes: Legalized prior invalid contract shape by replacing notes object with notes array and explicit top-level protocol sections.
Added incident_lifecycle, audit_events, authorization_matrix, failure_modes, detector_abuse_safeguards, restore_and_failover_semantics, and runtime_validation_requirements.
Kept C-mode manual approval posture while tightening release, restore, and abuse safeguards.
Hardening pass focused on detector abuse resistance, partial execution semantics, scoped session segmentation, release quorum, and runtime validation matrix.
Added event registry hooks and ERR-1 integration prerequisites without introducing premature subcode drift.
Extended edge cases and failure modes for impersonation misuse, duplicate incidents, device quarantine, and post-release regression.
Adds incident plane isolation matrix to replace vague where-safe language with explicit fail-closed boundaries.
Adds freeze queue policy, destructive operation classes, boot/readiness barriers, job execution barriers, and webhook ingest continuity rules.
Adds incident artifact sensitivity controls and hardens detector escalation and edge-case handling for signal storms and flash-sale incidents.
Adds readiness state model to prevent boot-barrier crash loops while keeping privileged surfaces deny-by-default.
Splits provider ingest into verified and unverified quarantine lanes during secret overlap or signature uncertainty.
Adds integration severance rules, signal volume circuit breakers, dual-privilege principal rules, and live-session revocation law.
Hardens job barriers, edge cases, and runtime validation matrix for in-flight work, external partner safety, and WAF/edge shedding posture.
Adds interactive upgrade barriers so degraded_alive nodes do not become zombie LiveView or WebSocket traps.
Adds quarantine replay side-effect policy and severance reconciliation requirements to prevent replay spam and unsafe reopen after severance.
Adds live-session revocation backpressure, edge-shedding observability requirements, leased-job incident barriers, and incident artifact export controls.

rules: IR-1 MUST be validated under chaos scenarios before any D-mode automation is enabled.
Chaos scenarios MUST include token replay waves, credential stuffing bursts, admin-takeover simulation, partial org containment, and key rotation under live load.
Chaos validation MUST prove: no money moves without journal, no payout release occurs during freeze, no cross-tenant containment leak, and no inventory truth corruption.

completion_layers.authoritative_complete: Durable authoritative state has been updated so future validations fail closed against compromised state.
completion_layers.propagation_complete: Required cache invalidation, fan-out, and cluster convergence acknowledgements have reached the required threshold for the affected plane.

rules: Containment execution MUST track per-operation-class status; partial completion MUST NOT be treated as effective full containment.
Release is forbidden while any mandatory success class for the approved tier remains incomplete, failed, quarantined, or awaiting compensation.
Compensation or retry-safe replay requirements MUST be recorded per incomplete operation class with owner, due_at_utc_or_null, and evidence_ref.

For operation classes marked forward_recovery_only or externally_destructive, compensation MUST mean forward recovery planning and completion tracking, not rollback of already-destructive external actions.

dependencies.reason: Schema source of truth for contract-suite/1.0, test-gates/1.0, and bundle-manifest/1.0.
Strict CI validation and deterministic assertion enforcement expectations for bundle legality and semantic gates.
Gate authoring discipline and test-gates structure used by IR-1.
Approval governance, break-glass controls, and sensitive-operation audit posture used by IR-1.
Signals, incidents, evidence, alerting, and runbook posture required by IR-1.
Deployment and migration safety gates that must honor active security incidents.
Session, step-up, MFA, and authorization capability primitives used by containment actions.
Assurance epoch semantics used for deterministic invalidation.
Key management and secret-rotation posture escalated during incidents.
Tenancy isolation rules that bound containment blast radius.
Lock ordering and idempotency constraints for containment workflows.
Performance budgets and chaos-readiness expectations for incident simulations.
Queue-capacity and admission and backpressure controls during containment mode.
Canonical error envelope and correlation semantics for blocked actions and incident responses.

examples: reject_immediately freeze on admin mutation surfaces
webhook secret rotation with external partner cutover
api key revoke plus local cache invalidation
provider integration isolated after forward recovery timeout
partner webhook lane severed into quarantine

rules: Containment operations MUST be classified before execution as reversible, forward_recovery_only, externally_destructive, or hybrid_external_internal.
Forward recovery, not rollback, is mandatory for externally destructive security operations.
Release and compensation logic MUST honor the destructive class of each executed operation.
If a forward_recovery_only or externally_destructive operation breaches timeout budget, integration severance MAY replace indefinite platform hostage posture where policy permits.

detector_abuse_safeguards: Signals MUST preserve vector_class, severity, affected_plane, and evidence novelty so deduplication cannot suppress materially different attacks.
Repeated triggers MAY be deduplicated only when scope, vector_class, severity, affected_plane, and lifecycle_state remain unchanged and no materially new evidence exists.
Higher-severity or different-vector signals MUST break deduplication and either escalate or fork incident handling according to lifecycle_state.
Cooling windows and suppression rules MUST be suspended when evidence quality, affected plane, or approved scope rises.
Tier 2 and Tier 3 escalation MUST still require corroborating evidence beyond a single detector family in C-mode unless break-glass rules explicitly allow otherwise.
Detector-only evidence MUST NOT trigger payout freeze or platform-wide credential invalidation in C-mode without human approval or break-glass.
If identical signal velocity exceeds the approved volume circuit breaker threshold, the application MUST stop per-event deduplication work and shift to aggregate telemetry plus edge shedding.

detector_escalation_controls.cooling_window_rule: Cooling windows MUST be defined in OBS-1 runbooks per signal family before detector-driven automation is enabled.
rules: Tier 2 and Tier 3 MUST NOT be reached from a single detector family alone in C-mode unless GOV-0 break-glass is invoked and justification is recorded.
Repeated triggers without materially new evidence MUST attach to the active incident for that scope rather than spawn parallel incidents.
At most one scoped revoke per approved scope per cooling window MAY execute from detector-driven escalation unless evidence quality rises and approval is refreshed.
If approved_scope exceeds suggested_scope or approved_tier exceeds the maximum default_tier of originating signals, justification MUST be recorded and post-incident review is mandatory.

If an incident is in eradication_in_progress or recovery_validation and a new higher-severity or different-vector signal storm hits the same scope, the system MUST fork a successor incident or escalate the existing incident; silent merge is forbidden.

If identical-scope identical-vector traffic crosses the approved volume circuit breaker threshold, application-layer deduplication MUST yield to aggregate accounting and edge mitigation; continued full per-event evaluation is forbidden.

If a principal holds any platform-level authority on the same auth surface implicated by the incident, partial org-scoped session invalidation is forbidden unless session segmentation proves the platform authority is fully separate.

When auth surface separation cannot be proven for a dual-privilege principal, IR-1 MUST require global session_revoke for that principal and full re-authentication before any privileged access resumes.
Platform-staff privileges MUST be evaluated as a higher-risk surface than org-only privileges when both coexist on the same principal.
Stateless bearer tokens that cannot be deterministically invalidated per approved scope MUST be treated as broader-scope compromise artifacts.

edge_cases: Multi-org principal holds admin access in org A and buyer access in org B; org-scoped revoke MUST not erase unrelated buyer continuity unless explicitly approved.
Offline scanner device is suspected compromised while disconnected; reconnect MUST trigger quarantine and replay review before post-incident trust is restored.

Incident occurs during flash sale; buyer continuity MAY remain available only if incident_plane_isolation_matrix explicitly allows it for the affected planes, otherwise checkout finalization MUST fail closed.
Session revoke succeeds but webhook secret rotation lags; incident remains open and release is forbidden until the lagging surface is closed or compensated.
Incident starts during payout run; payout release MUST fail closed if any affected scope is under active freeze.
Restore or failover occurs with active incident; containment state and regulatory clock continuity MUST survive restore.
Anomaly detector itself is abused to create self-DoS conditions; corroboration and re-trigger suppression MUST exist before higher-tier escalation.
Impersonation session is active during suspected compromise; containment and approval logic MUST treat impersonation surfaces as higher risk and MUST forbid their use as approvers.
Break-glass session itself is suspected compromised; incident MUST escalate to a scope that invalidates break-glass credentials or routes authority to unaffected approvers.
Org-scoped containment targets a principal who is also platform staff; platform privileges MUST be evaluated separately and MUST NOT silently survive if they share the compromised auth surface.
Webhook partner fails to rotate secret within overlap window; release remains forbidden until the affected ingress path is disabled, compensated, or re-scoped.
Duplicate incident creation occurs for the same signal storm; merge semantics MUST preserve evidence continuity and MUST NOT fork approval chains.
Post-release validation fails during quiet-period observation; a successor incident MUST inherit predecessor linkage and MUST re-apply required freeze posture.
Tier 3 revocation of large non-privileged session populations risks re-authentication thundering herd; containment MUST use staggered or jittered invalidation outside the privileged session class.
Cache invalidation fan-out lags authoritative revocation; privileged surface reopening MUST wait for required propagation completion rather than assuming durable mutation alone is enough.
Externally destructive key or secret rotation partially completes; forward recovery, not rollback, MUST drive the remaining workflow.
Frozen surfaces accumulate queue backlog; release MUST obey freeze_queue_policy rather than draining all queued work at once.
Webhook receipts continue arriving while downstream financial processing is quarantined; ingest MUST continue and replay disposition MUST be tracked before release.
Auto-scaling occurs during active Tier 3 incident; new nodes MUST survive in degraded_alive without false privileged readiness rather than crash-looping on readiness barriers.
Webhook partner continues sending payloads with stale secret during approved overlap; receipts MUST enter isolated unverified quarantine lane, not the primary ingest path.
Forward-recovery-only external rotation exceeds timeout budget; integration severance MAY isolate the dependency so unrelated surfaces are not held hostage indefinitely.
Identical same-vector signal storm exceeds application dedupe budget; edge shedding or WAF controls MUST activate before app-layer OOM or lock exhaustion occurs.
Production chaos simulation touches external partners; destructive external simulations MUST use sandbox or stub environments rather than live partner credentials.
Dual-privilege principal shares one auth surface across org and platform roles; partial revoke is forbidden unless segmentation is proven.
Long-lived admin WebSocket survives bearer token revocation window; live session revocation rules MUST force disconnect, downgrade, or heartbeat revalidation.

A degraded_alive node accepts a WebSocket or LiveView upgrade before authoritative incident posture is loaded; the upgrade MUST be rejected or redirected rather than trapping the client in a zombie UI.
Quarantined provider receipts are replayed after incident release; replay MUST reconcile silently by default and MUST NOT spam buyers or partners with duplicated side effects.
A severed integration becomes reachable again after a timeout; reopen MUST wait for severance reconciliation classes rather than assuming continuity.
Mass live-session termination would exceed scheduler or PubSub budgets; revocation MUST wave, batch, or jitter rather than self-DOS the cluster.
Edge shedding mitigates a signal storm during a flash sale; aggregate drop telemetry and collateral estimates MUST still reach central observability.
A job leased before freeze reaches pre-commit after freeze activation; the job MUST re-check incident posture before commit and follow a deterministic blocked disposition.

rules: Any WAF, CDN, firewall, or edge-shedding rule activated under incident posture MUST emit aggregate telemetry back into the central observability stack.
Aggregate telemetry MUST include at least rule_id, vector_class, scope_ref, dropped_request_count, time_window, and an estimate or classification of potential collateral impact.
Checkout- or event-facing edge controls SHOULD prefer richer selectors than raw IP-only thresholds when available so grouped legitimate buyers are not silently discarded at scale.
An attack MUST NOT disappear from internal observability merely because mitigation moved to the edge.
These labels are planning hooks only and MUST be registered in ERR-1 before implementation introduces subcode fields or user-visible mappings.
IR-1 MUST NOT introduce any JSON field named exactly subcode until ERR-1 registry entries exist and suite validation can prove membership.
Blocked-operation envelopes and containment failures MUST remain ERR-1 compliant even before dedicated IR labels are registered.

error_and_runbook_binding: Any user-visible block caused by containment MUST use ERR-1 compliant error envelopes with correlation_id.
Every signal family and containment operation class MUST map to an OBS-1 runbook identifier.
Runbooks MUST specify investigate, contain, validate, release, and post-incident review steps.

rules: These event names MUST be registered in EVT-1 before IR-1 is locked for implementation.
Implementation MUST NOT invent alternate event names for the same lifecycle steps.
Telemetry, audit, and post-incident evidence MUST use the same canonical event names or explicit mapped aliases recorded in EVT-1.

failure_modes.behavior: Reject action; return ERR-1 compliant blocked-operation envelope with correlation_id.
Fail closed; do not broaden target scope; require investigation update.

Record per-operation authoritative and propagation completion evidence, keep incident open, and require forward recovery, compensation tracking, or retry-safe replay according to destructive operation class.
Containment remains active until criteria pass; release attempt is audited.
No disruptive auto-escalation in C-mode; investigation required.
Incident freeze and evidence continuity MUST be reloaded before sensitive surfaces reopen.
Reject approval or release attempt; keep incident state unchanged; audit the violation and require alternate approver chain.
Fail closed; do not execute scoped containment until segmentation dimensions are complete or broader scope is explicitly approved.
Attach evidence only when scope, vector_class, severity, affected_plane, and lifecycle_state remain unchanged; otherwise fork or escalate incident handling.
Deny trust restoration for the device until offline evidence replay and reconciliation complete; keep incident or successor incident open.
Open successor incident, restore required freeze posture, and record predecessor linkage and failed validation evidence.
Apply declared freeze_queue_policy, drop or quarantine excess work with audit, and keep release blocked until backlog disposition is safe.
Keep node or process unready for privileged traffic, emit readiness failure telemetry, and forbid affected surfaces from reopening.
Preserve append-only receipt ingest, quarantine unsafe downstream processing, and require replay disposition before release.
Open successor incident or escalate existing incident rather than silently merging materially different attack vectors.
Use staged revocation or jittered re-auth controls for non-privileged sessions and keep incident active until auth load stabilizes within approved degraded mode.

bounded_queue_requirements: Queue entries MUST carry expires_at_utc and correlation_id.
Queue entries that outlive declared TTL MUST be dropped or quarantined according to surface policy; release MUST NOT drain stale backlog blindly.
Backlog replay after release MUST be rate-limited and jittered to avoid stampede behavior.
rules: A frozen surface MUST declare one of: reject_immediately, drop_with_audit, bounded_queue_with_ttl, or async_quarantine; implicit infinite queueing is forbidden.
Freeze queue behavior MUST be selected per surface and incident plane and MUST be recorded in incident evidence.
Release MUST verify that backlog handling completed according to the declared freeze policy before affected surfaces reopen.

surface_policies.reason: Avoid approval and config backlog explosions during active containment.
Money-moving requests MUST not silently queue during security containment.
Buyer-facing degraded mode MAY admit bounded request buffering only where correctness truth is intact.
Finalizing inventory or payment truth during affected planes is forbidden.
Provider receipts MUST ingest durably while unsafe downstream processing is quarantined.
Payload review MAY continue without restoring device trust.

implementation_order: P0 hygiene alignment to CS-0@2.3.0 across dependent bundles.
IAM-1 and IAM-3 and TEN-1 scope semantics for session revoke and epoch invalidation.
SEC-1 incident-tier binding for key and secret rotation.
PSC-1 and OBQC-1 chaos and admission hooks.

rules: Incident evidence bundles, timelines, and forensic exports MUST be treated as security-sensitive artifacts and MUST NOT inherit ordinary analytics or support export posture by default.
Export of incident artifacts MUST require step-up authentication, explicit authorization, bounded justification, encryption at rest and in transit, TTL-bound access, and immutable audit logging.
Exports MUST support redaction profiles so customer-facing or tenant-facing disclosures can exclude internal security posture, partner secrets, or unrelated-org evidence.
Org-facing disclosure of incident artifacts MUST default to curated summaries unless a stricter approval path explicitly authorizes raw forensic export.
Incident evidence bundles, approval records, signal details, and scope decisions MUST be treated as sensitive security artifacts, not generic analytics output.
Access to incident artifacts MUST be least-privilege, auditable, and export-controlled.
Incident artifacts MUST NOT be exposed to tenant-facing or public surfaces except through explicitly approved redacted summaries.
Retention and deletion policy for incident artifacts MUST respect legal hold, regulator-ready evidence requirements, and security sensitivity.

Incident artifacts containing quarantined provider payload references, severance decisions, or live-session disposition evidence MUST be treated as security-sensitive operational evidence and export-restricted by default.
Export or disclosure of incident artifacts MUST obey incident_artifact_export_controls and MUST be auditable as a security-sensitive export.
Every disruptive action MUST reference a stable incident_id and current lifecycle state.
State regression is forbidden except detected→triaged restarts caused by duplicate signal merge or restored replay, and such regression MUST be auditable.
Released incidents that fail post-release validation MUST open a new incident_id linked to the predecessor rather than silently mutating history.

states.meaning: One or more signals exist but scope and severity are not yet approved.
Incident record exists and provisional scope and tier have been assessed.
Human approver chain or break-glass has approved disruptive action.
Approved containment actions have executed and active freeze posture is in effect where relevant.
Underlying compromise path is being removed or rotated out.
Containment remains in force while evidence verifies system stability and safe reopen.
Containment has been lifted under explicit release criteria and audit.
Release occurred but post-incident review remains mandatory before closure.
Evidence package and review are complete.

examples: checkout queue state tied to inventory

rules: Containment decisions MUST classify the affected plane before buyer continuity or surface freeze decisions are approved.

If the affected plane includes inventory truth, seat allocation truth, payment confirmation truth, or shared warm state required for correctness, checkout finalization MUST fail closed regardless of buyer disruption.

If the affected plane is limited to privileged control surfaces and correctness truth remains uncompromised, buyer continuity MAY remain available under degraded mode with explicit approval and evidence.
Plane isolation decisions MUST be recorded per incident and MUST bind freeze_queue_policy and release decisions.

examples: Payment-provider webhook secret rotation stalls because partner fails to cut over; webhook processing for that integration is severed and quarantined while unrelated buyer browsing continues.
Third-party admin SSO key rotation stalls; admin SSO remains disabled while buyer auth and unaffected org scopes continue under approved degraded mode.
rules: If an external integration required by containment remains incomplete beyond its approved timeout budget, the platform MAY sever that integration scope rather than hold unrelated surfaces hostage indefinitely.
Severance MUST record the disabled integration surface, residual risk, customer or organizer impact summary, and the narrowed incident scope that remains frozen.
Severance MUST NOT relax containment on unrelated mandatory success classes; it only permits release of unaffected surfaces once the compromised integration is isolated.
A severed integration MUST remain blocked until separate recovery criteria are met and approved.
Release from severance MUST satisfy severance_reconciliation_requirements; severance alone is not sufficient to reopen affected surfaces.
integration_severance_rules.timeout_budget_rule: Each forward_recovery_only or externally_destructive integration operation MUST declare a timeout budget and severance owner before execution.

rules: A node in degraded_alive MUST NOT accept LiveView, WebSocket, SSE, or other long-lived interactive upgrades that depend on authoritative incident posture.
A node in buyer_limited_ready MAY accept only explicitly allowlisted buyer-facing upgrade routes whose authorization and mutation paths are proven safe for the current incident plane posture.
Interactive upgrade denial MUST return a generic temporary-unavailable boundary response with correlation_id and MUST NOT leak internal IR scope or tier labels.
Load balancer or ingress routing MUST be able to distinguish privileged_not_ready from hard-dead node posture so degraded nodes are not recycled solely for failing privileged readiness.
Authoritative incident posture, not cached posture alone, MUST be required before privileged interactive upgrades are accepted.

required_barriers.purpose: prevent new work on frozen surfaces from starting
stop external or irreversible effects once incident posture is active
prevent durable local commit after late-arriving freeze or revocation
prevent frozen surfaces from enqueueing work that will only die later under known active incident posture

rules: Jobs that can mutate money, inventory, membership, key material, or payout state MUST perform incident checks at pre_dispatch, pre_side_effect, and pre_commit boundaries.
A job leased before containment began MUST still fail closed if a later barrier detects active incident posture affecting its scope.
Barrier failures MUST produce auditable quarantine or retry decisions and MUST NOT silently complete side effects.
Jobs leased before containment and jobs spawned during containment MUST both honor barrier checks; in-flight work is not grandfathered past incident posture.
Barrier outcomes MUST distinguish retry, quarantine, sever, and hard-fail dispositions; indefinite silent retry loops are forbidden.
Leased jobs MUST additionally obey leased_job_incident_barriers when incident posture changes after lease acquisition.
Jobs already leased before an incident freeze or scope escalation MUST re-check incident posture before side effects and again before commit when the job can mutate sensitive surfaces.
A job leased under pre-incident posture MUST NOT be treated as trusted solely because it was dequeued earlier.

If an in-flight job becomes blocked by incident posture, it MUST enter a deterministic blocked disposition: abort_with_no_side_effect, quarantine_for_review, or retry_after_incident, as defined per job class.
Jobs affecting money, inventory, issuance, payout, membership, or security posture MUST implement pre-dispatch, pre-side-effect, and pre-commit incident barriers.
High-volume live-session revocation MUST be partitioned, jittered, or batched; single-shot global fan-out is forbidden when it would exceed scheduler, PubSub, or queue budgets.
Privileged session revocation MAY remain immediate when required, but non-privileged session revocation MUST respect backpressure budgets and approved wave sizing.
Revocation waves MUST emit progress metrics and backlog metrics so operators can distinguish completed revocation from merely scheduled revocation.
Revocation planning MUST preserve a dedicated control path for incident responders so the cluster does not self-lock by saturating all scheduler or message-queue capacity with disconnect traffic.
Long-lived sessions including LiveView, WebSocket, scanner streams, and admin subscriptions MUST define incident revocation behavior explicitly; HTTP-only revocation is insufficient.
For privileged or incident-affected live sessions, the default action MUST be immediate disconnect or downgrade to read-only according to approved plane policy.
Heartbeat or channel revalidation intervals MUST be short enough to make revocation effective within the approved risk window for the affected surface.
Live-session revocation decisions MUST emit telemetry linking session_id_or_channel_ref, incident_id, and resulting disposition.
Live-session revocation MUST obey live_session_revocation_backpressure and MUST NOT saturate scheduler or message fan-out budgets.

notes: v1.1.0 legalizes the prior invalid notes object by moving normative content into explicit top-level sections and protocol fields.
IR-1 is intentionally C-mode first: disruptive actions remain human-approved until D-mode graduation gates are satisfied.
IR-1 does not introduce ERR-1 subcodes yet; it declares required ERR-1 integration work without creating suite drift before ERR-1 is patched.

v1.2.0 hardening pass: added session segmentation law, atomicity and compensation semantics, approval distinctness constraints, release quorum, event and ERR-1 integration hooks, and runtime validation matrix.

v1.3.0 hardening pass adds plane isolation, queue freeze policy, forward-recovery doctrine, boot/readiness barriers, job execution barriers, webhook ingest continuity rules, and incident artifact sensitivity controls.

v1.4.0 hardening pass adds readiness state model, verified/unverified provider ingest lanes, integration severance rules, signal volume circuit breakers, dual-privilege principal rules, and live-session/job runtime protections.

v1.5.0 hardening pass adds interactive upgrade barriers, quarantine replay side-effect policy, severance reconciliation requirements, live-session revocation backpressure, edge-shedding observability requirements, leased-job barriers, and incident artifact export controls.
production_readiness_checklist: Incident IDs are stable, unique, and required before disruptive actions.
Signals include required correlation fields and evidence refs.
Scoped containment is supported for org, actor, role, and platform scopes as defined.
Disruptive actions are idempotent and audit-linked.
Payout freeze can be applied and released without bypassing finance integrity.
Runbooks exist for every signal family and containment operation.
Regulator-ready evidence package can be generated for Tier 2 and Tier 3 incidents.
Chaos scenarios are defined before D-mode automation is enabled.
Incident plane isolation matrix is implemented for all sensitive surfaces.
Freeze queue policy exists per frozen surface and backlog replay is bounded and rate-limited.
Boot and readiness barriers prevent privileged traffic before incident posture is loaded.
Webhook/provider truth ingest remains append-only during incidents and downstream quarantine is replay-safe.
Externally destructive containment operations use forward recovery, not rollback assumptions.

rules: IR-1 MUST support revoking org-admin sessions without revoking buyer sessions for unaffected orgs.
Every session_revoke action MUST be idempotent and record target_scope, target_selector, approval_ref_or_break_glass_ref, and correlation_id.
session_revoke MUST record whether buyer continuity, staff continuity, and platform-staff continuity were expected to remain available after execution.
step_up_force MAY be used before password or session invalidation as a lower-disruption control.
step_up_force MUST expire deterministically and MUST be auditable.
actor_assurance_epoch semantics from IAM-3 MUST be honored.
NEW proposed invariant: org_assurance_epoch and global_credential_epoch MUST exist before D-mode auto-escalation is enabled.
Epoch bumps MUST invalidate only scopes explicitly targeted by approved scope.
Key rotation MUST honor SEC-1 overlap windows and MUST NOT create unverifiable in-flight traffic.
Key rotation actions MUST record old_epoch_ref, new_epoch_ref, overlap_policy_ref, and completion evidence.
API key revocation MUST preserve evidence linking each revoked key to incident_id and approved scope.
Webhook secret rotation MUST provide overlap or explicit partner-facing cutover semantics; silent secret swaps are forbidden.
Freeze controls MAY block payout destination changes, refund execution, ticket transfers, org membership changes, or other high-risk surfaces defined by GOV-0 and OBS-1.
Freeze controls MUST map to ERR-1 compliant error envelopes and MUST emit active-incident evidence.
Payout freeze MUST be available whenever integrity, reconciliation, or security compromise makes payout safety uncertain.
A payout freeze MUST remain in effect until release criteria are met and evidence is attached.
payout_freeze MUST be idempotent per approved scope and MUST survive restore until explicit release is approved.

governance_posture: IR-1 MUST prefer scoped containment over platform-wide disruption when evidence supports bounded scope.
IR-1 MUST support C-mode now: tool-assisted investigation plus human approval for disruptive containment.
IR-1 MAY evolve to D-mode automation only after approved thresholds, evidence quality, and chaos validation exist.
investigation_workflow: Every incident MUST have a stable incident_id before any disruptive containment action executes.
Investigation MUST classify provisional scope as one of actor_scoped, org_scoped, role_scoped, multi_org, or platform_wide.
Investigation MUST record suggested_scope separately from approved_scope; suggested scope MAY be machine-produced, but approved scope MUST be human-approved in C-mode.
If evidence is insufficient to prove bounded scope, investigators MUST escalate one level higher rather than assume safety.

If approved_scope exceeds suggested_scope or approved_tier exceeds the highest default tier of originating signals, the approval record MUST include explicit justification and post-incident review owner.
release_criteria: An incident MUST NOT be released from containment until evidence shows targeted signals are stable or resolved, approvals are recorded, and blocked high-risk surfaces are safe to re-open.
Payout freeze release MUST respect existing finance integrity and reconciliation gates in V42 and OBS-1.
Release MUST be auditable and MUST record residual risk notes if any.
Release MUST verify all mandatory containment success classes for the approved tier are complete and no required compensation items remain unresolved.
Release MUST verify no pending device quarantine or offline reconciliation remains for scopes whose trust depends on device state.

tier_0_monitoring.intent: Normal posture with anomaly detection active and no containment action applied.
rules: Signals MAY be recorded and investigated without user-visible disruption.
Tier 0 MUST preserve enough evidence to support later escalation.

tier_1_scoped_suspicion.intent: Org-scoped or actor-scoped suspicion requiring fast investigation and limited reversible controls.
rules: Tier 1 MUST prefer actor-scoped or org-scoped actions over global invalidation.
Tier 1 MAY force scoped step-up auth, revoke org-admin sessions for an affected org, or temporarily freeze high-risk admin mutations within approved scope.
Tier 1 disruptive actions remain human-approved in C-mode.

tier_2_multi_org_or_admin_surface.intent: Evidence suggests compromise spans multiple orgs, shared admin surfaces, shared keys, or platform support paths.
rules: Tier 2 MUST permit role-scoped containment such as revoking privileged admin sessions, forcing recent step-up revalidation, freezing payout-destination changes, and rotating affected signing material.

Tier 2 MAY preserve buyer continuity only when the approved incident plane isolation matrix explicitly permits it; if the affected plane includes inventory truth, checkout finalization, payment confirmation, or shared warm state required for seat integrity, buyer checkout MUST fail closed.
Tier 2 disruptive actions MUST require dual approval unless GOV-0 break-glass criteria are satisfied.

tier_3_platform_compromise.intent: Evidence indicates platform-wide credential, key, session, secret, or infrastructure compromise.
rules: Tier 3 MUST allow global credential invalidation, global privileged-session revocation, platform-wide key rotation, webhook and API secret rotation, and payout freeze until integrity checks are green.
Tier 3 MUST be treated as SEV1 security posture for deployment and migration gating.
Tier 3 MUST record exact start time, scope, reason, approval chain, and release conditions.

non_goals: IR-1 does not define UI copy, legal advice, or customer communications templates.
IR-1 does not weaken V42 fail-closed posture, org_id isolation, payout safety, or immutable audit expectations.
purpose.one_liner: Bind signals, investigation, scope selection, containment operations, escalation, release, regulatory evidence, and chaos-readiness into one enforceable law.
scope: Detection signals, investigation workflow, scoped containment operations, escalation tiers, evidence capture, release criteria, regulatory reporting hooks, and chaos-readiness requirements.
Applies to platform-wide incidents and org-scoped incidents affecting identities, sessions, credentials, keys, API clients, payout safety, privileged operations, and device trust.

rules: Replays from quarantine MUST default to silent reconciliation paths that do not re-emit customer notifications, downstream partner callbacks, or derived side-effect jobs unless explicitly approved.
Replay mutation paths MUST be able to repair order, payment, ticket, seat, and ledger state without treating replay as a fresh business event.

If replay of quarantined payloads would cause externally visible side effects, those side effects MUST require explicit approval and MUST be emitted through a separately auditable replay side-effect lane.
Replay completion evidence MUST record whether reconciliation was silent, whether any side effects were intentionally emitted, and which customer- or partner-facing channels were suppressed.
Readiness MUST distinguish process liveness from privileged readiness; failing a privileged readiness barrier MUST NOT require orchestrator termination by default.
Orchestrator probes MUST tolerate degraded_alive and buyer_limited_ready states without killing the node, provided the node is not falsely advertising privileged readiness.
Release MUST NOT depend on cached readiness state alone; authoritative incident posture remains the source of truth.
Stale cached incident posture MAY keep a node in degraded_alive but MUST expire aggressively and MUST fail closed on ambiguity.

states.intent: Node remains process-alive and cluster-visible but MUST NOT advertise privileged readiness while incident posture is stale or unavailable.
Node may serve explicitly allowed buyer-safe degraded traffic once incident plane rules and freeze posture are loaded.
Node has loaded incident posture but MUST keep privileged surfaces disabled until propagation and barrier checks pass.
Node may serve all authorized traffic after incident posture, freeze posture, and runtime barriers satisfy required convergence.
Node is alive for liveness and limited degraded responses but MUST reject long-lived interactive upgrades until authoritative incident posture is loaded.

rules: IR-1 MUST capture a regulator-ready evidence package for Tier 2 and Tier 3 incidents.
Evidence package MUST include incident_id, timestamps, triggering signals, approved scope, executed containment operations, user or org impact summary, and release criteria.
IR-1 MUST track notification_decision_status separately from legal advice; the platform records evidence and timing, but legal determination remains outside this contract.
IR-1 MUST support a 72-hour reporting clock field for jurisdictions that require it; absence of a reporting obligation MUST be an explicit recorded decision.

release_quorum_requirements.minimum_quiet_period_rule: Quiet-period duration MUST be defined in OBS-1 runbooks per signal family before D-mode is enabled.
rules: Release MUST verify that all mandatory containment success classes for the incident tier are complete and auditable.
Release MUST verify a minimum detector quiet period appropriate to the signal family or must record an explicit override rationale under GOV-0 break-glass.
Release MUST verify no unresolved compensation items remain for required operation classes.
Release MUST verify no pending device quarantine or offline reconciliation remains for scopes whose trust depends on device state.
A post-release validation failure MUST open a successor incident linked to the predecessor and MUST NOT silently re-open the released incident.
Release MUST verify plane-specific convergence requirements, including authoritative_complete and propagation_complete where required, before affected surfaces reopen.
Release MUST verify backlog disposition under freeze_queue_policy and MUST NOT unleash accumulated requests without bounded replay controls.

restore_and_failover_semantics: Active incident state, approved scope, and active freezes MUST survive restore and failover before sensitive surfaces reopen.
Revocation completeness MUST be re-verified after restore for sessions, keys, secrets, and payout freeze posture.
Regulatory clocks and evidence package continuity MUST survive restore; restored incidents MUST NOT lose original opened_at_utc or first_signal_at_utc.
Restore and failover MUST reload incident freeze posture before sensitive write surfaces, payout release, or privileged approval surfaces become available.
Queue and admission posture associated with active incidents MUST be re-applied or explicitly revalidated after restore before traffic normalization.
Evidence, approvals, and notification decision refs MUST remain linked across restore or failover boundaries.
Processes and nodes recovering during an active incident MUST remain unready for incident-affected privileged traffic until boot_and_readiness_barriers are satisfied.

runtime_validation_matrix.pass_criteria: Replay suspicion signal emitted, scoped containment blocks target surface, unaffected scopes remain available, correlation_id preserved.
Detector deduplicates repeated triggers, C-mode avoids disruptive escalation without approval, and unaffected scopes stay usable.
Privileged mutation is blocked or contained, audit events chain correctly, and release remains unavailable until criteria pass.
Target org admin surface is contained while unrelated buyer continuity and unrelated org continuity remain available.
Rotation honors overlap policy, no unverifiable traffic occurs, and queue/backpressure posture remains within approved degraded mode.
Frozen surfaces do not queue infinitely, stale work is dropped or quarantined according to policy, and release replays only bounded safe backlog.
Recovered nodes remain deny-by-default until incident posture is reloaded and privileged surfaces stay unavailable until barriers pass.
New nodes survive in degraded_alive or buyer_limited_ready without advertising privileged readiness or entering orchestrator crash loops.
Verified receipts continue on the primary lane while stale-signature overlap receipts are isolated into quarantine and never mutate primary truth.
A stalled external forward-recovery operation can be severed without holding unrelated surfaces hostage, and severed scope remains explicitly blocked.
High-volume duplicate storms transition to aggregate accounting and edge shedding before application-layer OOM or lock exhaustion occurs.
A dual-privilege principal sharing one auth surface is globally revoked for that principal rather than silently retaining platform authority.
Privileged and incident-affected live sessions disconnect, downgrade, or force re-auth within the approved risk window.
Nodes lacking authoritative posture reject or redirect interactive upgrades instead of mounting zombie UIs.
Quarantine replay repairs state through silent reconcile paths and does not re-emit customer or partner side effects by default.
A severed integration cannot reopen until all applicable reconciliation classes are green and residual risk is recorded.
Live-session revocation respects batching or backpressure budgets and does not collapse scheduler or message fan-out capacity.
Edge shedding produces aggregate observability and collateral estimates rather than making the attack invisible internally.
Jobs leased before freeze re-check incident posture before side effect and commit, and blocked jobs enter deterministic dispositions.

runtime_validation_requirements: Static JSON gates are insufficient by themselves; runtime harness validation MUST prove telemetry emission, correlation integrity, freeze enforcement, and safe release behavior.
No D-mode automation may be enabled until runtime validation passes under representative load and failure injection.
Runtime validation MUST produce scenario-specific evidence artifacts defined in runtime_validation_matrix before IR-1 is considered implementation-ready.

session_scope_segmentation.fail_closed_rule: Any missing segmentation dimension required for approved scope MUST block the scoped containment action and record containment_selector_under_scoped_session_gap.
rules: Sessions, grants, and revocation selectors MUST be segmentable by actor_id, org_id when present, role_surface, and auth_surface before org-scoped or role-scoped containment is allowed.
If a principal session or grant cannot be deterministically segmented to the approved scope, IR-1 MUST fail closed and either escalate scope explicitly or deny the scoped action with audit.
Org-scoped revocation MUST NOT erase unrelated buyer continuity, unrelated org continuity, or non-target auth surfaces unless approved scope explicitly includes them.
Role-scoped revocation MUST use deterministic selector criteria; fuzzy matching or ad-hoc manual principal lists are forbidden.
Dual-privilege principals MUST not rely on partial token invalidation unless platform authority and org authority are cryptographically or session-issuance separated.
An integration severed under incident response MUST NOT reopen until the required reconciliation classes for that integration have completed and evidence is attached to the incident record.

Minimum reconciliation classes MUST include provider receipt reconciliation, internal ledger reconciliation where money moves, order or payment-intent reconciliation where commerce state is affected, and inventory or issuance reconciliation where tickets or allocations are affected.
Reopen decisions MUST record mismatch thresholds, residual risk, and whether any quarantined receipts remain unresolved.
If a reconciliation class is not applicable to a severed integration, the release record MUST explicitly state not_applicable with justification.
Deduplication MUST stop being per-event application logic once identical signal volume exceeds the approved edge or WAF transfer threshold for that vector and scope.

When volume circuit breaker activates, the system MUST switch to aggregate telemetry accounting and edge shedding or firewall enforcement rather than evaluating every duplicate in the application layer.
Circuit-breaker activation MUST preserve enough aggregate evidence to support incident review without requiring full packet-by-packet ingest.
Volume circuit breakers MUST break deduplication cooling windows immediately if severity, vector class, or affected plane rises.

summary: Tiered incident response law hardened for runtime survivability, including interactive upgrade barriers, quarantine replay suppression, severance reconciliation, live-session revocation backpressure, edge-shed observability, leased-job barriers, and security-sensitive incident artifact export controls.
title: IR-1 Incident Response and Containment Protocol

lanes.entry_condition: signature_or_auth_validation_passes under active approved secret and overlap policy
rules: Verified receipts MAY continue through normal durable ingest even when downstream processing is quarantined.

lanes.destination: isolated cold quarantine holding store separated from primary ingest pipelines
lanes.entry_condition: signature validation fails but the receipt falls within an explicitly approved overlap or severance investigation window for the affected integration
rules: Quarantined unverified receipts MUST NOT flow into normal processing or mutate money, inventory, or payout truth until cryptographic or equivalent provenance is proven.
Quarantine records MUST preserve raw payload evidence, arrival timestamp, candidate integration scope, and disposition owner.

lanes.destination: no primary ingest; retain only minimal safe rejection evidence
lanes.entry_condition: validation fails outside an approved overlap or severance window or payload is malformed beyond safe retention policy
rules: Rejected receipts MUST raise alerting and MUST NOT be silently accepted to satisfy ingest continuity language.
Ingest continuity during incident MUST distinguish verified and unverified payload lanes; accepting unverified partner payloads into the primary ingest path is forbidden.
Overlap windows MUST be explicitly approved, time-bounded, and tied to an incident or severance record.
Release of affected financial or webhook-dependent surfaces MUST verify all unverified quarantine receipts are dispositioned.
Any replay from unverified quarantine MUST obey quarantine_replay_side_effect_policy before mutating primary truth or emitting side effects.
Provider webhook or receipt ingest MUST remain append-only and idempotent during incidents; dropping provider truth is forbidden.
Verified receipts MUST continue through the verified_primary_ingest lane; unverified overlap-window receipts MUST be diverted to isolated quarantine and MUST NOT reach normal processing.
Unsafe downstream processing MAY be quarantined, but receipt preservation MUST continue with evidence linking each receipt to incident posture decisions.
Release MUST verify quarantined provider receipts were replayed, superseded, severed, or dispositioned according to policy before affected financial surfaces reopen.
